{"world_model":"W5 (contrarian), after E034. The tip is E034: 9.25 true epochs (232 steps at batch 2000), 20/24/28/32 px at 30/10/30/30%, and a group-1 freeze for the last 25% of steps. It runs 5.481 s and scores 0.7539 on seeds 0–2. It passed the held-out gate of ≥0.7545.

1. Settled by reading the code:
- Muon has no wd, and the filters are renormalized every step, so H1.5.4 is settled. Newton-Schulz already runs 3 steps.
- Images already travel as uint8 and are normalized on the GPU. Whitening already uses 5k images.
- The whitening-bias lr goes to 0 at 3 epochs (75 steps, about 32%), but its backward keeps running until the freeze at 75%.
- MaxPool comes before BN in every group. So group-1 BN runs on 15×15 maps, not 31×31. Only conv1's output and the pool see 31×31 traffic. This shrinks the value of BN folding (I057).
- prepare's eigh, pad and randperm are not warmed in build. That is the likely source of trial 0's extra ~0.15 s, worth about 0.05 s on the 3-trial mean.

2. Where the stem's cost sits (my new mechanism). E028 saved about 15 ms per truncated 32 px step, about 27% of the step for about 20% of MACs. That cost is not BN. It is conv1's 31×31×128 fp16 output and its backward: pool backward scattering into a 31×31×128 map, then wgrad and dgrad of conv1 at full resolution. These are bandwidth-bound. Levers that avoid the backward through conv1's 31×31 output pay well (freeze dose, I055). Levers that touch only the 24-channel whitening map (I054) or the 15×15 BN (I057) pay little, about 1% each.

3. Chaotic decorrelation (E029, E030, E032). Any change to the dynamics re-rolls the per-seed outcomes. The re-draw centres on the population mean plus the true effect, with a 3-seed SD of about 0.15 pp. "Neutral" structural changes cost about 0.1 pp on average. Math-identical systems changes (I053) should reproduce per-seed results exactly, with drift of 0.03–0.05 pp at most.

4. Time model. Fixed host and optimizer overhead is roughly 5–8 ms per step. Large-map steps cost more than their MAC share. Step removal and stem truncation pay about 1.5× what MAC models say. My range misses have all been on the high side of the measurement, so I keep biasing time forecasts low.

5. Resolution. Early low resolution is nearly free (E026, E033). The 28/32 tail and the jump into 32 px carry the accuracy (E011, E018, E024).

6. Dials:
- Epochs: 0.25 epoch ≈ 0.13 s ≈ 0.12 pp.
- Freeze at 25%: about 0.8 s for about 0.2 pp.
- Freeze dose to 40%: probably about +0.35–0.45 s saved for about 0.25–0.35 pp. Group 1 then stops during the 28 px phase and never adapts to 32 px. That is still about the same rate as the epoch dial or a bit better, so freeze 60% plus an epoch top-up may land near 5.25 s.

7. Muon. Its benefit on CIFAR-100 short runs is probably real, at 0.3–0.8 pp. SGD at batch 2000 with linear lr scaling is probably worse than E005's SGD. Dropping Muon saves only about 2–3% of time.

8. Noise:
- 3-seed mean: SD about 0.15 pp.
- 10-seed held-out mean: SE about 0.08 pp.
- Winner's curse on seeds 3–12: about 0.05–0.1 pp. I expect fresh seeds 13–22 at about 0.7535–0.754.

Unsure:
- How the host-overhead and bandwidth shares split. I058 should settle it.
- Transfer of bandwidth-bound levers to the PCIe judge, whose HBM bandwidth is about 1.9 vs 2.0 TB/s. That is close, so transfer is probably fine.

W5 (contrarian), after E034. The tip is E034: 9.25 true epochs (232 steps at batch 2000), 20/24/28/32 px at 30/10/30/30%, and a group-1 freeze for the last 25% of steps. It runs 5.481 s and scores 0.7539 on seeds 0–2. It passed the held-out gate of ≥0.7545.

1. Settled by reading the code:
- Muon has no wd, and the filters are renormalized every step, so H1.5.4 is settled. Newton-Schulz already runs 3 steps.
- Images already travel as uint8 and are normalized on the GPU. Whitening already uses 5k images.
- The whitening-bias lr goes to 0 at 3 epochs (75 steps, about 32%), but its backward keeps running until the freeze at 75%.
- MaxPool comes before BN in every group. So group-1 BN runs on 15×15 maps, not 31×31. Only conv1's output and the pool see 31×31 traffic. This shrinks the value of BN folding (I057).
- prepare's eigh, pad and randperm are not warmed in build. That is the likely source of trial 0's extra ~0.15 s, worth about 0.05 s on the 3-trial mean.

2. Where the stem's cost sits (my new mechanism). E028 saved about 15 ms per truncated 32 px step, about 27% of the step for about 20% of MACs. That cost is not BN. It is conv1's 31×31×128 fp16 output and its backward: pool backward scattering into a 31×31×128 map, then wgrad and dgrad of conv1 at full resolution. These are bandwidth-bound. Levers that avoid the backward through conv1's 31×31 output pay well (freeze dose, I055). Levers that touch only the 24-channel whitening map (I054) or the 15×15 BN (I057) pay little, about 1% each.

3. Chaotic decorrelation (E029, E030, E032). Any change to the dynamics re-rolls the per-seed outcomes. The re-draw centres on the population mean plus the true effect, with a 3-seed SD of about 0.15 pp. "Neutral" structural changes cost about 0.1 pp on average. Math-identical systems changes (I053) should reproduce per-seed results exactly, with drift of 0.03–0.05 pp at most.

4. Time model. Fixed host and optimizer overhead is roughly 5–8 ms per step. Large-map steps cost more than their MAC share. Step removal and stem truncation pay about 1.5× what MAC models say. My range misses have all been on the high side of the measurement, so I keep biasing time forecasts low.

5. Resolution. Early low resolution is nearly free (E026, E033). The 28/32 tail and the jump into 32 px carry the accuracy (E011, E018, E024).

6. Dials:
- Epochs: 0.25 epoch ≈ 0.13 s ≈ 0.12 pp.
- Freeze at 25%: about 0.8 s for about 0.2 pp.
- Freeze dose to 40%: probably about +0.35–0.45 s saved for about 0.25–0.35 pp. Group 1 then stops during the 28 px phase and never adapts to 32 px. That is still about the same rate as the epoch dial or a bit better, so freeze 60% plus an epoch top-up may land near 5.25 s.

7. Muon. Its benefit on CIFAR-100 short runs is probably real, at 0.3–0.8 pp. SGD at batch 2000 with linear lr scaling is probably worse than E005's SGD. Dropping Muon saves only about 2–3% of time.

8. Noise:
- 3-seed mean: SD about 0.15 pp.
- 10-seed held-out mean: SE about 0.08 pp.
- Winner's curse on seeds 3–12: about 0.05–0.1 pp. I expect fresh seeds 13–22 at about 0.7535–0.754.

Unsure:
- How the host-overhead and bandwidth shares split. I058 should settle it.
- Transfer of bandwidth-bound levers to the PCIe judge, whose HBM bandwidth is about 1.9 vs 2.0 TB/s. That is close, so transfer is probably fine.
- Whether 40-seed accuracy stays above 0.75 for the tip. I think it does, with about 0.3 pp of headroom.

forecasts.reason: uint8 and the 5k subset are already in place, so only the eigh/cusolver warm-up in build remains: a ~0.04 s mean gain, right at the 0.05 s bar. Accuracy should be bit-identical.
The detach removes only the 24-channel whitening-map backward and conv1's dgrad (small Cin): about 1% over 55% of steps, below the 2% bar. Changing the bias LR re-rolls the seeds.
35 more truncated steps at ~11–15 ms each easily beat the 3% time bar. But freezing during 28 px means group 1 never adapts to 32 px, so the loss is likely 0.2–0.35 pp, near the 0.15 pp limit.
With no recipe change, seeds 0–2 repeat. On fresh seeds I expect about 0.7537 (a winner's curse of ≤0.1 pp), with the pooled mean ≥0.753.
Pool comes before BN, so group-1 BN runs on 15×15 maps and is cheap and already fused: under 1% saving. Switching to eval-mode BN with noisy momentum-0.4 stats risks accuracy.
E028's ~27% per-step saving implies group 1 plus whitening is ≥35% of the step. The non-GEMM share is likely ≥30%, dominated by conv1-output, pool and GELU traffic at 31×31.
Muon's renormalized, orthogonal updates matter at batch 2000 with ~230 steps. SGD with linearly scaled lr likely loses ≥0.4 pp, while the time saving is only ~2–3%.

cruxes: Where does the stem's per-step cost sit? I say it is conv1's 31×31×128 output plus the pool backward, and wgrad/dgrad, not BN or the whitening map. The I058 profile decides whether the freeze dose (I055) is the only stem lever worth running, with I054 and I057 skipped.
For the 60% freeze, is the held-out loss above or below ~0.3 pp, given that group 1 stops before seeing 32 px? Freezing later inside the 32 px phase (e.g. 70%) may be the better dose.

How much of the step is fixed host/optimizer overhead (eager fused SGD, a separate Muon graph, Lookahead foreach, Python LR loops) vs GPU compute? If it is ≥10%, one captured graph per step is a lever nobody has proposed, worth ≥0.3 s.
